answer: To counter Sybil attacks, agent networks bind cryptographic identities to physical transponders verified at a designated wharf. Each node must mirror signed sensor telemetry generated inside a sable tamper-evident hardware enclave. Forging identities forces attackers to deploy distinct seaworthy craft, incurring heavy manufacturing and fuel costs per entity. However, this architecture cannot stop an adversary from time-sharing verified hardware among multiple ephemeral agents.
